To make artificial intelligence a trusted, everyday capability of the Bank: to prove its value with the functions that serve our customers, to set the standard by which the Bank adopts it, and to keep every use of it accountable to people, so that the Bank serves its customers better, works with greater confidence, and leads with care.

AICC is the internal consulting and innovation lab of the Bank for the adoption of artificial intelligence. It explores and proves the use of AI with the functions of the Bank, delivers measured outcomes, and sets the way in which the Bank adopts AI at scale, with accountability that stays with people.

AICC serves the functions of the Bank. A function brings a need, AICC commits to an Engagement, delivers a Solution with its evidence, and supports it at the agreed level. The Business Model states the offer, and the Engagement workflow shows how a function works with AICC.

AICC works by one method: Initiatives are taken in and decided in the Portfolio, Solutions are delivered, released, and operated through the Solution Lifecycle, and the work runs on a common cadence and is measured. The workflows show the flow, and the guides explain it.

AICC is a joint team, led by the AICC Lead and formed of the people whom the functions of the Bank assign to it. Seven Roles carry the work, decisions are taken at defined levels, and the Steering and the Board Committee advise and oversee. The charter names Roles; the persons who hold them are recorded in the Appointments Record of the Registry.

The Bank uses AI under rules that are proportionate to risk. Each Solution has a Risk Tier, is checked or validated before use, and is overseen by people who can stop it. The AI Policy states the rules, the Risk Tiers, the review of providers, the handling of AI Incidents, and the Exceptions, within the AI Risk Appetite Statement of the Bank.

AICC is controlled, reported, and assured through five control loops, a catalogue of thirty-two controls, and the records that evidence them. The AICC Lead reports each quarter, the Executive Sponsor issues the report to the Board Committee, and internal audit gives independent assurance. The status of each control at a date is kept in the Control Matrix of the Registry.
The thirteen templates are the forms of the records that AICC produces, from the Initiative Brief to the Quarterly Report. A template gives the form; the rules for the record are in the documents.
The Vocabulary defines the terms of the charter, the Document Catalog lists its documents, the change history records their revisions, and Records and systems states where each record is kept.
